Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
9 October 2026 .
Brent $ 104.93 + 0.28 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 A second commercial vessel was struck inside the Persian Gulf in three days, per gCaptain, though this has not been independently confirmed.

02 The IRGC claims it hit a large LPG tanker south of the Strait of Hormuz, sparking a fire, per Iranian state media; the US has not confirmed the strike.

03 The US sanctioned 17 vessels for transporting Iranian crude, oil products and petrochemicals, per MarineLink.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial traffic, with IMF PortWatch recording 4 transits on October 4 against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. The dominant operational story is a sustained pattern of vessel strikes inside and around the strait. gCaptain reports a second commercial vessel was struck by a projectile inside the Persian Gulf on Friday, sparking a fire; that report has not been independently confirmed. Separately, Iranian state media claim IRGC naval forces hit a large LPG tanker south of the strait, causing it to catch fire; CENTCOM has not confirmed that strike. The New Region also carries the earlier report, now attributed to multiple desks, that Iran struck a Vietnamese vessel in the strait. Yeni Safak English, Caspian Post, and others report tankers struck mines in or near the strait, citing Iranian state broadcaster IRIB, though no major wire in this feed carries the claim independently. On the policy front, Tehran's Friday prayers leader said, per Iranian state media, that the strait will remain closed until Iran's conditions are fully met by what he called the enemy. The IRGC, per IRNA, claimed US forces bear responsibility for maritime escalation, announcing a separate fire incident on a tanker. Brent crude stood at $104.93, up 0.28% over 24 hours, as of 15:24 UTC. The feed indexed 29 headlines in the past 24 hours. As of 15:20 UTC, 197 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
